title: Krishna eats the last leaf
hook: the pot is empty, a famously angry sage is coming, and Krishna arrives asking for food; why Hindus offer food to God first
carry: a leaf offered with love is enough for God

segments.voice: Yesterday, the householder's work is dharma at home: asked for a charm, she gave a list of chores and remembered keeping the accounts at Indraprastha.

Dinner is over. The plates are washed. The cook has finally sat down and eaten her own meal. Then there's a knock. A great sage is at the door, with a crowd of disciples behind him, and they would like to be fed. They're going down to the river to bathe first. They'll be back soon. Hungry. In the forest years of the Mahabharata, this is Draupadi's evening, and the sage is Durvasa, remembered for his temper and his curses. Today: an empty pot, and the guest who scraped it.
screen: `THE MEAL IS OVER.` → `A SAGE AT THE DOOR, WITH DISCIPLES.` → `AN EMPTY POT.`

segments.voice: First, the pot. Early in the exile, the sun gives Yudhishthira a vessel that will feed the household and its guests every day, until Draupadi has eaten. So Draupadi serves everyone first and eats last. Some tellings carry the next part. Duryodhana, hoping to trap his cousins, sends Durvasa at exactly the wrong hour, after Draupadi has eaten. The sage and his disciples go off to bathe. Draupadi has nothing to give them, and a sage refused hospitality might curse the house. So she turns to Krishna in her mind, and Krishna arrives. His first words, in paraphrase: I'm hungry. Give me something to eat. The pot is empty, she tells him; that's why I called you. He asks to see it anyway. Stuck to the rim is one small scrap of cooked greens, a bit of leaf. Krishna eats it, and says, may this satisfy the one who is the soul of the world. Down at the river, the sages suddenly feel full, as if they'd eaten a feast, and slip away. Here's the teaching. In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna says it plainly, in paraphrase: whoever offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water with love, I accept it. In this story he shows it: one leaf, from a woman with nothing left, and the soul of the world is satisfied. That's why, in many Hindu homes, a little of the meal is set before God first, naivedya, and then shared as prasad, blessed food. The size of the offering was never the point.
screen: `A VESSEL THAT FEEDS UNTIL SHE EATS` · `KRISHNA COMES ASKING FOR FOOD` · `ONE LEAF ON THE RIM` · `A LEAF, A FLOWER, A FRUIT, WATER`

segments.voice: At your next meal, before the first bite, set aside a small portion, a spoonful, a piece of fruit, and offer it silently, the way many Hindu families do; then eat it or share it as prasad. Some families say a short verse from the Gita before eating, brahmarpanam, offering the meal back to God; others simply say Krishna's name. If you don't pray, just pause and thank everyone whose work is on the plate.
Draupadi. When the pot was empty and guests were coming, Krishna made a meal of the one leaf on its rim. Today's word.
Your line: a leaf offered with love is enough for God. Krishna ate the last one. I'll be here tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus hear the story of Durvasa's visit in retellings of the Mahabharata and in devotional storytelling; and in many homes a little food is offered to God before the meal, then shared as prasad.

Durvasa.meaning: a sage the stories remember for his temper and curses

Yudhishthira.meaning: the eldest Pandava, given the sun's vessel

Mahabharata.meaning: the great epic of the Pandavas and their cousins

naivedya.meaning: food offered to God before it is eaten

prasad.meaning: offered food, shared afterward as a blessing

brahmarpanam.meaning: a Gita verse many recite before meals: the offering is God's

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parvan), Yudhishthira receives a vessel from Surya (Critical Edition 3.3; Ganguli section 3)

notes: The Durvasa episode is found in the vulgate Vana Parva (Ganguli 261–263) but, as far as the writer knows, is not in the body of the Critical Edition; the voice says 'some tellings of the epic carry the next part'. Please confirm.

Confirm the details: Duryodhana sends Durvasa to arrive after Draupadi has eaten; Krishna says he is hungry; a particle of vegetable or leaf on the rim; Krishna's words about satisfying the soul of the universe; the sages feel full while bathing and leave.
The vessel's rule (it gives food until Draupadi has eaten) is from Vana Parva 3; year 3 day 777 told the gift of the vessel from Yudhishthira's side, so this day keeps that brief.
'akshaya patra' as the vessel's name is common in later retelling; the voice does not use it. Check the original-game note and Devanagari.
